judgements.reason: Bridge to Reasoning. reasoning_given states only the demand half ('open labs keep shipping sparse frontier-scale weights far beyond what enthusiast memory can hold'), and four consecutive bridges now show the demand half strengthening while every shipped answer takes a competing route: validation.89b8dba663cd3ba4 (2026-07-19) 'Moonshine reaches usable local speech by building small rather than by paging a large model'; validation.96fe3259cd716f12 (2026-07-20) 'SGLang's wide expert parallelism spreads experts across a datacenter fabric, not off disk into a local runtime'; validation.4e59ca3ae9fd796f (2026-07-24, dim=landing) 'Two of the four named runtimes shipped this week and neither carried the feature'; and this week's validation.693121d262f24853 (2026-07-31 benchmark, 2026-08-02 row) 'no offload of any kind appears - nothing streams cold experts from host memory or disk'. The reasoning bundle carries no trace of the three rival mechanisms (shrink-the-model, spread-across-a-fabric, hold-it-all-in-HBM) that are actually shipping, so it cannot state what would distinguish its route from theirs. This accumulating counter-signal is invisible to the scoring layer: all 5 evidence links for this prediction are support_direction='support' with contradiction_score=0.0, as are all 8258 links project-wide, so the spec's Bridge-to-Reasoning contradiction rule could never have fired here. First-time stale for this prediction - no prior maintenance-update marker exists for it in any week.

All 5 bridges read correctly against their sources and the relevance track (5, 3, 3, 2, 2) honestly records a founding datapoint followed by adjacent-but-not-confirming evidence. This week's validation.693121d262f24853 is the freshest and is self-critical about it ('The measurement cuts the other way on the remedy'). Two structural defects are attached to the stream rather than to its content, and neither is prediction-specific: (a) contributes_to_task_id is NULL on this bridge and on all 1808 validation_rows project-wide, so the spec's Bridge-to-Needs correlation ('a bridge cited an actor delivering on a Need's task.what') has no wiring anywhere and had to be reconstructed by reading bridge text; (b) the 2026-08-02 row renders to readers with its literal '[REVIVED]' prefix - confirmed at future-prediction/en/future-prediction-20260802.md line 37, one of 12 such occurrences in that file - on a row whose own body ends 'No local runtime shipped a streaming feature today'. Content verdict is fresh; the two defects are escalated separately.

Applies to the whole Need-set. All four needs (need.708171f0c16abe6e, need.bcbb82def269d3af, need.092850c920d697fd, need.c319aa474086132c) carry target window 2026-07-01..2026-12-31, which closes on 2026-12-31 - the day before the prediction's own target window (2027-01-01..2027-06-30) opens - while every one of their tasks states when='H2 2026 through H1 2027'. The structured windows contradict the task text and expire before the landing they are meant to enable. Needs to Reasoning: nothing in the Need-set has been delivered, and the bridge record agrees (validation.4e59ca3ae9fd796f, 2026-07-24: 'No release note from llama.cpp, Ollama...'), so this is a window-authoring defect, not a delivery event. needs_tasks.status cannot corroborate either way: it is 'open' on all 1167 rows project-wide and 'done' has never been written.

Edge-extraction outage, not a healthy stream. This prediction has zero prediction_chain rows and zero prediction_relations rows in either direction. That is not a property of the prediction: prediction_chain holds 127 rows whose created_at range is 2026-06-09T18:25:42Z..2026-06-10T10:34:13Z and prediction_relations holds 200 rows all stamped 2026-06-09T18:25:42Z, so no edge of either kind has been written project-wide in roughly eight weeks, and only 48 and 52 of 324 predictions carry any chain or relation edge respectively. Escalate as a pipeline outage; a per-prediction rewrite cannot fix it and marking this stream 'fresh' would launder the outage into per-prediction health.

Bridge to Reasoning, on two clauses now. The 2026-07-19 run judged this stale and wrote app/sourcedata/2026-07-19/maintenance-update.reasoning.prediction.1ce328e19c9e6685.json with a replacement 'given'; it was never applied - the DB still reads reasoning_given='only captive owners have both the capital to buy a robot maker and the in-house demand to run it', and the marker's replacement text appears nowhere in the row. That clause is still contradicted by validation.2fd74050bb4f0f6a (2026-07-18, relevance 4): Toyota ran Walden Robotics machines in its own North American plant from February and then took minority equity, which the bridge itself calls 'a customer underwriting a supplier, not a captive fleet' - an actor with both the capital and the captive demand that chose partner-not-acquire. Since that unapplied verdict a second clause has been hit: validation.28509240c3f7bca4 (2026-07-28, relevance 4, dim=so_that) reports the only humanoid operating-hours figure disclosed that week - 65,000+ hours across nine customer facilities plus $300M of Digit v5 orders - accrued by a merchant maker selling into other people's sites, which is the third-party RaaS outcome reasoning_so_that says will lose, while no captive fleet disclosed anything. Four bridges, all accurate against their cited sources, and the two most recent are candid where the evidence runs against the thesis - validation.2fd74050bb4f0f6a separates the sequencing that holds from the ownership form that diverges, and validation.28509240c3f7bca4 states plainly that 'a captive owner has no customers to count'. Needs to Reasoning: need.19b68be950704991 is already historical. Its job - 'Executing the ownership-consolidation buyout that absorbs the robot maker whole when the venture IPO exit fails' - is written prospectively but describes the event that is the prediction's own reasoning_because: SoftBank took its put-option exit and Hyundai absorbed 100% of Boston Dynamics. Its task need_task.64787b0fa80f6dac says when='At the IPO-deadline put-option exit window, mid-2026 onward', a window that has already run. Per the spec's Needs-to-Reasoning rule this Need should be reframed forward to the NEXT precondition (converting whole ownership into installed captive units), not left standing as an outstanding ask. Two of the three needs on this prediction (need.19b68be950704991, need.cc59bb6c01119d19) additionally carry NULL target_start_date and target_end_date on both the need and its task, so neither can be windowed or aged. Eight bridges spanning 2026-07-11 to 2026-07-30, each grounded in a dated, linked source, with relevance tracking the actual distance from the claim (5 for the AI Now origin and the Mindgard disclosure, 3 for adjacent vectors such as MemGhost's email-and-memory path, which the bridge itself flags as 'not a repository audit'). Flagging one merge-layer hazard rather than a content problem: _stale_applied (app/skills/weekly_maintenance.py:722) treats a bridge judgement as already applied if app/sourcedata/<week>/bridges.json merely contains the prediction id, so any bridge-stream rewrite for a prediction that received a bridge that day would be silently marked done - verified live for prediction.16c7b8053e39aa1f in this week's bridges.json.

Bridge to Needs: need.31fd8de6a99f8cbd has been half-delivered and its text cannot express that. Its job is 'Converting existing sandbox, permission-prompt, and allowlist pieces into a default-deny, network-isolated execution mode for untrusted-repo review', and validation.65ebc6d2f4157099 (2026-07-17, relevance 4) documents Claude Code v2.1.212 shipping exactly the generic half by default - Bash permission checks failing closed on file-descriptor redirect forms, a Windows PowerShell 5.1 bypass closed, commands over 10,000 characters always prompting, default-on session caps - while the bridge itself notes 'this is general permission hardening, not a dedicated untrusted-repo audit sandbox'. The Need should be split so the delivered generic hardening is recorded and the outstanding ask is the untrusted-repo-specific audit mode named in its own outcome. Nothing in the data would have surfaced this: contributes_to_task_id is NULL on this bridge and all 1808 validation_rows, and needs_tasks.status is 'open' on all 1167 rows project-wide, so the delivery had to be read out of the bridge text.

Bridge to Reasoning. reasoning_so_that asserts that CISA, FDA, NHTSA and ENISA publish joint disclosure-and-remediation guidance, and the newest bridge is a direct observation of the opposite: validation.4d1ed88cbce397cd (2026-07-28, relevance 4, dim=so_that) records two AI-found or AI-assisted flaws surfacing on the same day into 'entirely different disclosure regimes, with nothing connecting them' - HAWK producing a standardisation problem with no identifier at all, CVE-2026-53264 carrying a CVSS 7.8 and backports to seven stable lines but 'no KEV entry, no cross-sector advisory, and public exploit code'. That is the prediction's own stated bear case (parallel-but-unreconciled sectoral responses) showing up as the observed default, and the four-clause reasoning bundle carries no hedge for it. Separately, reasoning_given rests on three forcing functions - EU CRA 2027 in-force, the FDA 2027 refresh, the CISA Secure by Design pledge - and across the only three bridges this prediction has ever received (2026-06-01, 2026-06-06, 2026-07-28) nothing touches the pledge programme or the FDA refresh; the one institutional datapoint, the June 6 executive order's AI Cybersecurity Clearinghouse, is a different vehicle than the one reasoning_landing names ('four-authority MoU or joint advisory'). Reframe given and landing to the mechanism the evidence actually shows moving.

The three bridges (2026-06-01, 2026-06-06, 2026-07-28) are each accurate against their sources and the newest is the most rigorous of them, refusing to score a non-connection as support. No rewrite needed. Recording the coverage gap rather than treating it as a content fault: this prediction has drawn three bridges in the nine weeks since 2026-05-30, with a seven-week silence between 2026-06-06 and 2026-07-28, so the evidence base under a Q3 2027 four-authority claim is thin by volume rather than by quality.

Bridge to Reasoning on landing and given; the 2026-07-26 stale verdict was never applied and five new bridges have since sharpened the case. reasoning_landing reads 'By H1 2027; two-plus threat-intel vendors or a MITRE ATT&CK technique', and validation.8b87ea3a3d9ed16a (2026-07-30, relevance 5, dim=landing) shows why that wording now mis-scores the claim: 'The landing condition asks for two vendors, and today supplies the second: Sysdig's ransomware account earlier, Palo Alto Networks' campaign reconstruction now. What neither supplies is a name for the class.' As written the clause is satisfiable by two publications, which have now happened, while the actual claim - a named, documented detection category - has not; the landing must be re-pinned to the naming act rather than the publisher count. reasoning_given ('Agents weaponize known, cataloged CVEs within the hours-long patch window CISA's sprint exposed') is separately undercut twice: validation.5a2902415a41f31a (2026-07-31, relevance 5) states 'no vulnerability identifier appears anywhere in the account, and the compromise ran on credential theft and SQL injection, techniques no patch window governs', and validation.2b74e0d99bda31cc (2026-08-01) records a stolen long-lived Tailscale auth key enrolling 181 nodes with 'no exploited flaw, no rushed use of a catalogued vulnerability'. The cataloged-CVE patch-window premise is not the mechanism the observed intrusions used. The DB text is unchanged from before app/sourcedata/2026-07-26/maintenance-update.reasoning.prediction.3049b69e910c2279.json, so this is a live defect, not a duplicate.

The densest and best-behaved bridge stream in this batch: 15 rows from 2026-07-09 to 2026-08-01, each tied to a dated, linked source, and the relevance track rises with the evidence (5 for the JADEPUFFER origin, then 4s across the Hugging Face attribution arc, then 5s for the Unit 42 and Hugging Face technical-timeline artefacts).
